overclaims: The evaluations used different GPT-4 deployments or snapshots.
checks.note: The excerpt, proposition, the 'may be in place' hedge, the outcome (supported, conclusive_event) and the citations all check out. The problem is one limitation, which states as fact that the evaluations used different GPT-4 deployments or snapshots. No evidence item identifies a snapshot or deployment for e2 or e3. The evidence only shows different timing: the jailbreak result was present in May 2023, and XSTest responses were collected on 2023-09-18. Suggested rewording: say the tests ran at different times and may have used different snapshots.

The proposition 'GPT-4 will eclipse ChatGPT and attract even more attention' drops 'totally' from 'totally eclipse', so it understates the speaker's commitment. That matters because the contract and support condition depend on 'substantially more' attention, and the public proposition no longer conveys that strength. Everything else is fine: the excerpt, the 'when it comes out' condition, the rationale (release per e1, no comparative measurement, no deadline), the outcome (unresolved, open_horizon) and the citations.
